goal: Say what you can do: 我会说中文, 你能来吗？

blocks.text: 会 (huì) and 能 (néng) both mean *can*, but for different reasons. Both go right before the verb.

blocks.h: 会: can, because you learned it

blocks.text: 会 is for skills: languages, cooking, driving, swimming. German has the same word for it: *Ich kann Chinesisch*.

blocks.h: 能: can, because you're able to or allowed

blocks.text: 能 is about the situation: you have the time, you're well enough, it's allowed.

wrong: 会 goes right before the verb: 我会说中文.

blocks.tip: 会 also means *will* (他会来的, *he'll come*). That's G56.

exercises.explain: Coming today isn't a skill you learn: 能. (你今天会来吗 would be *Will you come today?*)
不能 goes right before the verb.
